gaps.gap: Matthew and Luke both embed a prior-speech citation of Jesus in connection with the resurrection announcement; Mark alone provides the announcement with no prior-speech grounding.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M17 codes a prior speech-act by Jesus 'now cited' as a fulfillment tag syntactically attached to the announcement at M16 ('just as he said'). LUKE-24:M13 commands the women to remember; M14 reports the prior telling; M17 quotes the third-day rising as part of the cited passion prediction. MARK-16:M19 carries the resurrection announcement with no comparable authorization from Jesus's own prior words — M28 (the Galilee citation) authorizes the reunion commission, not the resurrection claim. Matt and Luke thus provide a double warrant — accomplished fact plus pre-authorized prediction — while Mark's announcement stands on angelic report alone. Consequential for QUD: in Mark, the attestation is thinner by one entire layer of grounding.

gaps.gap: No account describes what the raised state consists of — all three withhold the nature, quality, or phenomenology of the resurrection.
gaps.why: Every carrying account announces that Jesus has been raised / has risen / stands in the raised state without specifying what that state entails: whether bodily, spiritual, transformed, continuous with the pre-crucifixion body, or otherwise. MARK-16:M19's 'stands in the state of the raised' approaches an ontological framing but still withholds all content. LUKE-24:M12's 'he is alive again' gives the barest functional description. The announcement is uniformly thin on what is actually being announced beyond the bare propositional claim. Directly consequential for QUD: all three accounts attest the raised status while universally withholding what the status they are attesting consists of.

all_gaps_by_beat.beat: the witnesses are invited to view/verify the vacated burial spot

gaps.gap: No account records the propositional content the witnesses extracted from the verification — what seeing the vacant spot established for them is withheld by all.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M18-M19 commands approach and seeing but records only departure and doubled affect (M27-M28), no stated inference. MARK-16:M21-M23 commands looking but records only flight and ongoing fear (M29-M30), no stated conclusion. LUKE-24:M3-M4 records the empty-tomb discovery but codes the aftermath as perplexity (M5) and, after Peter's viewing, unresolved amazement (M28) — neither resolves into stated understanding. JOHN-20:M22-M23 records that the beloved disciple 'sees and believes' but both verbs are used absolutely without stated object, and M24 immediately glosses the entire male-disciple visit by noting they did not yet understand the scripture. The beat's evidentiary function — verification that establishes something — is universally withheld at the propositional level. Directly bears on QUD: the witnessing the accounts construct never closes the inferential gap it opens.

gaps.gap: John alone records that viewing the vacant spot produces belief in a witness; Matt, Mark, and Luke record no belief-outcome from the verification.
gaps.why: JOHN-20:M22-M23 records the beloved disciple taking in the interior scene absolutely and arriving at a state of belief — the vacant spot is explicitly causally linked to an epistemic outcome in one witness. MATT-28:M27-M28 records the women departing with fear and great joy but no stated belief from the viewing itself. MARK-16:M29-M30 records terror and flight, no belief. LUKE-24:M28 records that Peter is amazed in a state explicitly unresolved into belief or disbelief. John alone makes the verification epistemically productive in a named faith-state. Consequential for QUD: in three of four accounts, the verification attests the emptiness but generates no stated attestation of what it means; John alone closes that gap in one witness — while still withholding the propositional content of the belief.

gaps.gap: Matthew and Mark carry an explicit figure-issued directive commanding the witnesses to approach and look at the vacant burial spot; Luke and John carry no such directive.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M18 directs the women to come to the place of Jesus's laying; M19 directs them to see the spot — the figure constructs and initiates the verification act. MARK-16:M21 directs the women already inside to look at the burial spot — the figure frames and targets the looking. In LUKE-24, the two figures' entire speech (M9-M13) contains a rhetorical challenge, an absence declaration, a resurrection announcement, and a memory directive, but no command to look at or approach the spot; the women had already discovered the absence independently (M3-M4). In JOHN-20, no figure directs any witness toward the spot at any stage; the male disciples' viewing (M9-M22) is self-initiated, and the angels' address to Mary (M31-M32) is a question, not a verification directive. Consequential for QUD: in Matt and Mark the figure certifies the verification by commanding it, making the numinous authority co-sponsor the attestation; in Luke and John the verification is self-initiated, carrying no figure-directed authorization.

gaps.gap: John and Luke carry the textile arrangement (linen wrappings, head-cloth) as the evidentiary content of the vacant spot; Matthew and Mark carry only the bare location with no residual physical detail.
gaps.why: JOHN-20:M13-M14 and M18-M19 record that witnesses see the linen wrappings lying in position; M20 records the head-cloth rolled separately apart from them — a specific material arrangement persisting at the former body-site. LUKE-24:M26 records Peter seeing the linen cloths lying by themselves inside. MATT-28:M19-M20 cites 'the place where Jesus lay' as a bare location marker; no physical trace is described. MARK-16:M21-M23 refers to the spot demonstratively ('where they laid him') without naming any physical residue. The textile-arrangement detail carries a qualitatively different evidential claim: something about how the wrappings remain testifies to the manner of departure (a body removed by others would likely displace wrappings); the bare-empty-spot testifies only that the body is absent. Matt and Mark make the absence the entire evidence; John and Luke make the state of the grave-clothes a further witness.

gaps.gap: John alone has male disciples as the primary agents who view the vacant spot; Matthew and Mark direct the invitation exclusively to women; Luke has women as primary discoverers with a male disciple in secondary position.
gaps.why: JOHN-20:M9-M22 stages the primary verification entirely through Peter and the beloved disciple: they race to the tomb, enter, and inspect the spot; no female witness participates in this primary viewing. MATT-28:M18-M19 and MARK-16:M21 address the verification directive specifically to the women at the tomb, making female witnesses the figure-authorized verifiers. LUKE-24 carries women as the original discoverers (M3-M4) and Peter as a secondary self-initiated verifier (M24-M26), a two-stage structure. John's primary attestation of the vacant spot thus rests on male-disciple testimony with no figure directing them, while Matt and Mark rest it on female testimony that is figure-authorized. Consequential for QUD: the social-epistemic weight of the attestation differs across accounts depending on which witness-type is positioned as the primary verifier of the empty tomb.

gaps.gap: Matthew alone codes the verification as a two-step directed sequence (approach the place, then see it); Mark gives only a perception directive to witnesses already at the spot.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M18 directs the women to come toward the burial place — a positional movement — and M19 then separately directs the act of seeing: verification is constructed as a two-phase approach-plus-perceive sequence, implying the women are not yet at the spot when the directive is given. MARK-16:M21 gives only the perception directive ('look at the spot') to women who are already inside the tomb (M11), presupposing no positional movement is needed. In Matt the figure engineers not only what is seen but where the witnesses must be to see it; in Mark the engineering is purely optical. Consequential for QUD: Matt's architecture places the figure in the role of guiding the witnesses bodily into the evidential position, making the attestation more fully figure-constructed than Mark's version where the witnesses self-position and are only directed in their looking.

all_gaps_by_beat.beat: a prior word of Jesus is invoked to frame what has happened

gaps.gap: Luke alone invokes a prior word encompassing the full passion sequence (betrayal, crucifixion, and resurrection); Matthew invokes only the resurrection content; Mark invokes the Galilee commission.
gaps.why: LUKE-24:M13-M17 commands the women to recall a prior word covering hand-over (M15), crucifixion (M16), and third-day rising (M17) — the full arc of the passion. MATT-28:M17 invokes prior speech only on 'the raising-content later borne out,' bypassing the suffering phase entirely. MARK-16:M28 invokes a prior word whose content is not the passion prediction at all but the Galilee commission. Luke's scope transforms the resurrection from an isolated anomaly into the climax of a divinely necessitated sequence; Matt and Mark invoke prior words that do not construct that sequenced necessity. Consequential for QUD: Luke's invocation reframes what the resurrection attests — not only that Jesus is raised but that every step from betrayal onward was foreknown and foretold.

gaps.gap: No account specifies the original occasion, audience, or setting in which Jesus spoke the cited prior word.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M17 is coded as 'prior speech-act by Jesus, now cited' with no occasion specified. MARK-16:M28 is 'prior telling' whose original setting is not made recoverable in the move. LUKE-24:M14 is 'he told (reporting-speech, past)' with no occasion, audience, or location coded in the move. All three accounts invoke the prior word as a free-floating citation unanchored to a recoverable original context. Consequential for QUD: a prediction whose original occasion cannot be traced within the account is not independently verifiable as a prediction rather than a post-hoc construction. The prior word is deployed as attestation but withholds the conditions for confirming it was truly prior.

gaps.gap: Luke alone recovers the full content of the prior word in reported speech; Matthew gives a bare summary reference; Mark's content is explicitly unrecoverable.
gaps.why: LUKE-24:M14-M17 reproduces the substance of what Jesus said: hand-over, crucifixion, and third-day rising are each coded as distinct prior moves. MATT-28:M17 gives only 'the raising-content later borne out' — the content is implied but not spelled out. MARK-16:M28 is explicitly coded as 'content of the prior telling not made recoverable here.' Luke grants the witnesses (and readers) access to the substance of the cited word; Matt gestures at it; Mark withholds it entirely. Consequential for QUD: only in Luke can the reader check the current events against the specific terms of the prior prediction; in Matt and Mark, the prior word is cited as authority without the citation being checkable.

gaps.gap: Luke alone issues a figure-directed command to the witnesses to remember the prior word, and alone records the witnesses successfully executing that memory act.
gaps.why: LUKE-24:M13 is a directive to remember addressed to the women; M18 records the women's memory act as accomplished — the prior word's invocation is a two-stage cognitive transaction (command + execution) in which the witnesses become active retrievers of the citation. MATT-28:M17 appends the prior word as a tag on the angel's announcement without any move recording witness cognition in response. MARK-16:M28 cites the prior word as commission authorization without any move recording whether the women received or processed the citation. Luke uniquely makes the women participants in the evidentiary act of recall rather than passive recipients of a cited authority. Consequential for QUD: in Luke, the attestation is partly owned by the witnesses through their act of memory; in Matt and Mark, it remains entirely on the figure's authority.

gaps.gap: Mark alone invokes the prior word as authorization for a future appointment (the Galilee reunion); Matthew and Luke invoke the prior word retrospectively to interpret events that have already occurred.
gaps.why: MARK-16:M28's 'as he told you' is syntactically appended to M26-M27 (Jesus goes ahead to Galilee; you will see him there) — the prior word authorizes a future meeting, directing attention forward. MATT-28:M17's 'just as he said' is a retrospective fulfillment tag on the resurrection announcement (M16), pointing backward to confirm what has already occurred. LUKE-24:M14-M17's passion prediction is a hermeneutic frame for completed past events (betrayal, crucifixion, resurrection). Mark alone deploys the prior word prospectively, as warrant for what the disciples are now to expect; Matt and Luke deploy it retrospectively, as validation of what has just happened. Consequential for QUD: in Mark, what Jesus said governs the future of the attestation; in Matt and Luke, it governs the interpretation of the past — the testimonial orientation of the prior word is temporally inverted across the accounts.

all_gaps_by_beat.beat: the witnesses depart from the tomb

gaps.gap: Mark codes the departure as ending in complete silence — the commission is not carried out; Matthew and Luke code the departure as leading directly to commission execution.
gaps.why: MARK-16:M29 codes the departure as flight; M31 explicitly negates speech to any addressee ('they said nothing to anyone'); M32 closes the account in ongoing fear — the departure ends in a sealed silence. MATT-28:M27-M29 codes departure as purposive motion toward the disciples to deliver the message; the commission is in the process of being executed at the account's close. LUKE-24:M19-M20 codes return followed immediately by the women telling the eleven. The accounts are directly incompatible on what the departure produces: in Mark the tomb encounter issues in silence and withheld testimony; in Matt and Luke it issues in active testimony transmission. Directly bears on QUD: how the resurrection was attested depends entirely on whether the first witnesses to the empty tomb actually spoke — and the accounts contradict each other on this.

gaps.gap: John alone retains a witness at the tomb after the primary departure; Matthew, Mark, and Luke code complete withdrawal of all witnesses.
gaps.why: JOHN-20:M26 codes Peter and the beloved disciple returning home; M27 immediately codes Mary Magdalene standing weeping outside the tomb — she does not depart. In Matt (M27), Mark (M29), and Luke (M19), the departure is total: all present witnesses leave and the tomb scene ends. John's counter-departure move (M27) means the tomb-as-site-of-attestation remains occupied and continues to generate testimony after the male disciples' withdrawal. The subsequent angelic encounter (M29-M36) and the appearance of the risen Jesus to Mary are only possible because John withholds her from the departure. Consequential for QUD: John alone extends the chain of attestation at the tomb beyond the departure by leaving one witness in place.

gaps.gap: Matthew alone codes great joy as a component of the departure affect; Mark, Luke, and John code no positive affect at departure.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M28 codes 'fear and great joy' as a held compound state — the departing witnesses carry both simultaneously. MARK-16:M30 codes 'terror and amazement' and M32 closes with fear — no joy is registered. LUKE-24:M28 codes Peter's unresolved amazement, without positive valence. JOHN-20:M26 codes the disciples' return home without any coded affect. Matt's joy is not merely a textural variant; it changes the evidential character of the departure. Witnesses departing in joy are positioned to be credible carriers of good news; witnesses departing in fear (Mark) are positioned as traumatized and silenced. Consequential for QUD: the affective state in which the attestation chain begins diverges sharply — in Matt, the departure inaugurates testimony; in Mark, it forecloses it.

gaps.gap: Matthew alone embeds commission delivery as the explicit purpose of the departure motion itself; Mark codes departure as flight away from the tomb; Luke and John code return without embedded purpose.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M21 codes the departure as an urgent directed command; M29 codes the departure motion as 'purpose-embedded' — the running is already the commission in progress. MARK-16:M29 codes 'flee from the tomb,' a motion directed away from rather than toward any destination, with no commission purpose embedded in the motion itself. LUKE-24:M19 codes 'return' as a bare motion away from the tomb, with commission delivery (M20) coded as a separate subsequent event. JOHN-20:M26 codes 'return home' — toward lodgings, not toward disciples, with no commission context. Matt uniquely makes the departure and the commission execution a single purposive act. Consequential for QUD: in Matt the attestation chain is set in motion by the departure itself; in the others the departure is not yet the attestation.

gaps.gap: Matthew and Mark carry a figure-issued directive commanding the witnesses to depart; Luke and John have witnesses depart without any figure's command to leave.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M21 is an explicit 'go' directive coded as urgent and issued by the angel. MARK-16:M24 is a 'go' imperative issued by the young man in white. In both, the departure is commanded by the numinous figure before it occurs. LUKE-24:M19 codes the women returning with no preceding directive to leave — M13 commands memory, but no departure command is coded. JOHN-20:M26 codes the disciples returning home with no figure-issued departure command anywhere in the sequence. Whether the departure is figure-authorized or self-initiated changes the structure of the attestation: in Matt and Mark the figure sponsors not only the message but the act of leaving with it; in Luke and John the witnesses self-authorize their departure.

gaps.gap: No account records any speech or deliberation among the departing witnesses during the departure transit itself — the journey away from the tomb is narrated as motion and affect, never as interpretive dialogue.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M27-M29 codes departure as motion, affect, and running — no speech between the women en route. MARK-16:M29-M32 codes flight, gripped terror, and silence; M31 explicitly negates speech, but to any addressee, not specifically to each other. LUKE-24:M19 codes return as bare motion; M27-M28 code Peter's departure and unresolved amazement with no transit speech. JOHN-20:M26 codes return home with no recorded discourse during the journey. The departure is the moment at which witnesses who have just encountered an empty tomb and numinous figures are in transit — precisely the interval when interpretation would be expected to begin. All accounts withhold this transit-speech entirely. Consequential for QUD: the passage from tomb-encounter to community testimony is universally narrated as a gap, leaving unattested the witnesses' first unmediated attempts to make sense of what they had seen.

all_gaps_by_beat.beat: the witnesses are commissioned/moved to report to the (male) disciples

gaps.gap: John codes the report to male disciples as containing a theft/removal hypothesis; Matthew, Mark, and Luke code the commissioned message as containing (or implying) the resurrection announcement.
gaps.why: JOHN-20:M5-M8 codes Mary's report as: 'they took away the Lord; we do not know where they laid him' — a theft hypothesis with epistemic uncertainty about the body's location. No resurrection content is present. MATT-28:M22-M23 commissions a message that explicitly includes the raised-from-the-dead status. MARK-16:M25-M26 commissions a message whose content implies Jesus's active movement ahead to Galilee (presupposing he is alive). LUKE-24:M20 records the women telling 'the entire prior sequence at the tomb,' which carries the resurrection announcement (M12). The accounts directly contradict each other on what content moved male disciples to investigate the tomb: in Matt/Mark/Luke the witnesses carry an interpreted resurrection-event; in John they carry an uninterpreted disappearance-problem. Consequential for QUD: the initial attestation chain from tomb to male disciples carries fundamentally different epistemic content depending on the account.

gaps.gap: John alone has the witnesses' report to male disciples precede any interpretive encounter at the tomb — the report triggers the male disciples' visit rather than following from an already-interpreted encounter.
gaps.why: JOHN-20:M4-M5 codes Mary running to Peter and the beloved disciple and reporting before any figure appears to her — she acts on seeing the open tomb alone (M2-M3). Her report at M5 then causes the male disciples to set out (M9), and Mary's encounter with figures (M29-M36) only occurs after the male disciples have already returned home (M26). In MATT-28 and MARK-16, the figure's speech (M10; M15) precedes any commission to report (M22; M25) — the witnesses are first given an interpreted framework, then commissioned. In LUKE-24, the figures speak (M9-M13) and the women remember (M18) before they return and tell (M19-M20). John alone structures the beat so that the report is pre-interpretive — the witnesses report a puzzle, not a revealed event. Consequential for QUD: in John the attestation to male disciples begins without angelic interpretation; in the other three it begins from within an interpreted framework supplied by the figures.

gaps.gap: Matthew and Mark carry a figure-issued commission explicitly directing the witnesses to report to the disciples; Luke and John carry no such figure-directive — the reporting is self-initiated.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M21-M22 codes the angel issuing an urgent 'go' directive and a 'tell' directive specifically addressed to the women, naming the disciples as recipients. MARK-16:M24-M25 codes the young man issuing 'go' and 'tell' imperatives to the women. In both, the figure co-authors the commission. LUKE-24:M19 codes the women returning as self-initiated motion; M20 codes their telling as self-initiated speech — the figures' utterance (M9-M13) includes no go-and-tell directive to disciples. JOHN-20:M4-M5 codes Mary running and reporting on her own initiative, without any figure having directed her to do so. Whether the transmission chain is figure-authorized or self-initiated changes the epistemic structure of the attestation: in Matt and Mark the numinous figure sponsors the report as part of the commission; in Luke and John the report is the witnesses' own decision.

gaps.gap: Luke alone records the reception of the commissioned report as explicit apostolic disbelief; the other three accounts withhold or do not reach the reception.
gaps.why: LUKE-24:M22 codes the apostles classifying the women's testimony as 'an idle tale' — a category-denial of its evidential status; M23 codes explicit credence-refusal. The first act of attestation-transmission is met with institutional rejection. MATT-28:M29 closes while the women are en route — no reception is coded. MARK-16:M31 codes the commission's failure before delivery (short ending), so no reception is possible; the longer ending records delivery (M33) but no coded reception response. JOHN-20:M9 codes the male disciples' action-response (running to the tomb) but no evaluative or credal response. Luke alone makes the transmission's reception a datum in the attestation record, and makes it a datum of failure. Consequential for QUD: the canonical chain of resurrection attestation runs, in Luke, immediately through a disbelief event — the testimony is refused before it is accepted.

gaps.gap: Matthew alone marks the commissioned message with an explicit self-attribution of angelic authority; Mark, Luke, and John carry no such authority-marking on the commission.
gaps.why: MATT-28:M26 codes the angel attributing the entire message to its own angelic source — 'the message marked as coming from this angelic authority.' The commission thus carries a built-in credential: its origin is the figure who rolled the stone and sits enthroned on it. MARK-16:M25 issues the tell-directive without any self-attribution move. LUKE-24:M20 records the women telling what they witnessed without any figure attributing the report to its angelic source. JOHN-20:M5 is Mary's own self-initiated report. Matt uniquely builds an authority-chain into the commission itself: the message is credentialed at the source, not only at the content level. Consequential for QUD: in Matt the attestation carries its own provenance-marker; in the other accounts the commissioning figure does not sign the message.

gaps.gap: No account records any verbal response from the disciple-recipients upon receiving the report — the speech of the receiving disciples in the moment of attestation is universally withheld.
gaps.why: MATT-28 closes while the women are running toward the disciples (M29) — no reception scene is coded. MARK-16's short ending never reaches delivery; the longer ending records delivery (M33) but codes no response from Peter's circle. LUKE-24:M22-M23 codes apostolic evaluation (idle tale) and credence-refusal as states of mind, not as coded speech addressed back to the women — no dialogue is rendered. JOHN-20:M9 codes Peter and the beloved disciple setting out for the tomb as their response — action without recorded speech. Every account withholds what the disciples actually said to the messengers in the transmission moment. Consequential for QUD: the reception of the first oral link in the attestation chain is universally unnarrated as dialogue — the witnesses' testimony is delivered into a silence the reader cannot hear.

all_gaps_by_beat.beat: the announcement is (or is to be) carried to Peter and the wider disciple circle

gaps.gap: Mark (short ending) codes the announcement as failing to reach Peter and the disciples at all; Luke and John code it as successfully reaching its recipients.
gaps.why: MARK-16:M31 explicitly negates delivery — the women say nothing to anyone; M32 closes in fear with no commission executed (short ending). LUKE-24:M20 codes the women's telling as accomplished fact, with the eleven and the rest as named receivers. JOHN-20:M5 codes Mary's saying-to as delivered and received by Peter and the beloved disciple. all_gaps_by_beat.beat: a promise of future seeing/reunion with the risen Jesus is issued

all_gaps_by_beat.beat: male disciple(s) go to the tomb to verify the women's report

gaps.gap: John alone stages the beloved disciple's deliberate hesitation before entering — arriving first but deferring entry to Peter — as a distinct narrative move; Luke codes no approach-staging for Peter.

gaps.gap: Mark codes fear as the persistent unresolved closing affect; Luke codes amazement without fear, explicitly unresolved into belief or disbelief but not fear-valenced.

Consequential for QUD: in Mark the unresolved state produces a specific behavior (silence, flight); in Luke the unresolved state produces no behavior — it is a pure cognitive suspension. The nature of the gap between the tomb-encounter and full belief differs: in Mark it is affective blockage; in Luke it is epistemic indeterminacy.

Luke's closing state has a specified object even as the epistemic outcome remains suspended. Consequential for QUD: Luke's unresolved state is traceable to its evidential source; Mark's is not. The attestation gap in Mark is more radical — not only is belief withheld, but the grounds of the withholding are also withheld.

gaps.gap: No account specifies what epistemic event or experiential condition would be sufficient to resolve the unresolved closing state into full belief.

Neither account names the condition whose fulfillment would close the gap — neither the women's fear nor Peter's amazement is given a threshold. This is directly consequential for QUD: both accounts construct the resurrection as attested-up-to-a-point-but-not-yet-believed, and both withhold the specification of what 'fully believed' would require as evidence. The reader is given the unresolved state without a map of its resolution conditions.
